flagship.headline: Neil Diamond sings Sweet Caroline on The Ed Sullivan Show
flagship.summary_line_1: Neil Diamond performed Sweet Caroline and Holly Holy on The Ed Sullivan Show on November 30, 1969, per the show's official site and AllMusic.
flagship.summary_line_2: He sang Sweet Caroline sitting on a stool and returned to sing Holly Holy on top of a multicolored pyramid, and the clip below is his Sweet Caroline from the show.

events.headline: Neil Diamond sings Sweet Caroline on The Ed Sullivan Show
events.summary_line_1: Neil Diamond performed Sweet Caroline and Holly Holy on The Ed Sullivan Show on November 30, 1969, per the show's official site and AllMusic.
events.summary_line_2: He sang Sweet Caroline sitting on a stool and returned to sing Holly Holy on top of a multicolored pyramid, and the clip below is his Sweet Caroline from the show.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play the West Palm Beach festival
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played the West Palm Beach International Music and Arts Festival at Palm Beach International Raceway on November 30, 1969, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: The show was added to their American tour while it was already under way, and the clip below is Honky Tonk Women, their 1969 single.

events.headline: The Jimi Hendrix Experience play Cobo Hall in Detroit
events.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience played Cobo Hall in Detroit on November 30, 1968, with Cat Mother and the All Night Newsboys in support, per the official Jimi Hendrix encyclopedia.
events.summary_line_2: Their double album Electric Ladyland had reached shops weeks earlier, and the clip below is their 1968 cover of Bob Dylan's All Along the Watchtower.

events.headline: Bob Dylan records Can You Please Crawl Out Your Window?
events.summary_line_1: Bob Dylan is generally dated to November 30, 1965 for the session in Columbia Studio A in New York that produced the single version of Can You Please Crawl Out Your Window?, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Some Dylan scholars argue for an earlier date, Columbia released the single on December 21, 1965, and the clip below is the mono single version.

events.headline: Brian Epstein appears on Desert Island Discs
events.summary_line_1: Brian Epstein's appearance on the BBC radio series Desert Island Discs was first broadcast on November 30, 1964, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The Beatles manager had been in the national spotlight for a year by then, and the clip below is A Hard Day's Night, the title song of their 1964 film.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Empire Theatre in Sunderland
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Empire Theatre in Sunderland on Saturday, November 30, 1963, their second appearance at the venue after February 9, 1963, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It came a day after their Huddersfield dates and eight days after With the Beatles reached shops, and the clip below is It Won't Be Long, the album's opening track.

events.headline: Paul McCartney and Pete Best are deported from Germany
events.summary_line_1: Paul McCartney and Pete Best were deported from Germany on November 30, 1960, the day after Hamburg police arrested them on suspicion of arson, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The arrest followed a complaint about a fire at the Bambi Kino, and the clip below is My Bonnie, which the Beatles recorded in Hamburg with Tony Sheridan the following year.
